title: Reasons to stay natural: being a good role model
summary: NH argues that staying natural is partly a duty to the young lifters who look up to you. Undisclosed PED users give advice that does not work for naturals, which breeds blackpill discouragement and, when they are exposed, a loss of love for bodybuilding itself. Natural role models show the path is open.
claims: Being a good role model is one of the main reasons NH chose to stay natural, because people follow your example whether you want it or not
PEDs are objectively bad for your health and your finances and not advisable, especially for young men
The most visible fitness influencers are enhanced, making them unrelatable role models for young natural lifters
Training advice from enhanced lifters barely applies to naturals because they could not get big naturally themselves
Enhanced lifters' diets do not apply either; some cut fats almost completely, which would crush a natural's testosterone
Despite decades of bodybuilding culture and free information, young men are getting smaller and more discouraged because their role models are fake natties
The mainstream idea that natural gains end after two years and the blackpill mentality come from following undisclosed PED users whose advice did not build their physiques
NH's own role models were fictional, not real people
Everyone can get a good body naturally; it is not mainly a matter of genetics or god-given talent
Natural lifters who make it inspire others by showing the path is possible
When fake natties are exposed or get sick and lose their gains, followers lose love both for them and for bodybuilding itself, which is why it has a bad reputation
Bodybuilding in the 1950s was about health and building a godlike body; it was lost to drugs, supplement marketing and bad programs
Bodybuilding can only be reclaimed through natural role models who show their methods
